terms.definition: A plot of the correlation between a series and a lagged copy of itself, for lag 1, 2, 3, and so on. A slow decay suggests a trend or a non-stationary series. A sharp cutoff after lag q suggests an MA(q) model.
A test for a unit root. The null hypothesis is that the series is non-stationary. A small p-value (for example below 0.05) is evidence that the series is stationary.
A score that rewards a good fit and penalizes extra parameters. When you compare models on the same data, the model with the lower AIC is preferred.
A model in which today's value depends on a weighted sum of the p previous values plus noise. AR(1) uses only yesterday's value.
A model with three parts: AR terms (p), differencing (d), and MA terms (q). It is written ARIMA(p, d, q). The d value is the number of times the series is differenced to make it stationary.
A model that combines AR and MA terms. It is ARIMA with d = 0, so it needs a stationary series.
A score like AIC with a stronger penalty for extra parameters. It tends to choose simpler models than AIC. A lower value is better.
A range around an estimate, such as a model coefficient, that would contain the true value in a stated share of repeated samples. Do not confuse it with a forecast interval.
Replacing each value with its change from the previous value. First differencing removes a trend. Seasonal differencing subtracts the value from one season earlier.
An outside series, such as temperature, that you give to the model to help explain the target series. In SARIMAX it is the X.
The number of future steps that you ask the model to predict. Errors usually grow as the horizon gets longer.
A range around a forecast that is expected to contain the future value in a stated share of cases, for example 95 percent. The range widens as the horizon grows.
A step back in time. Lag 1 is the previous observation. Lag 7 in daily data is the same weekday one week earlier.
A test of whether the residuals still hold autocorrelation. The null hypothesis is that they do not. A large p-value is a good sign: it means the model left no pattern behind.
A model in which today's value depends on the q most recent forecast errors. It is not the same as a moving average used for smoothing.
The average size of the forecast errors, ignoring their sign. It is in the same units as the data.
The average size of the forecast errors as a percentage of the actual values. It is unreliable when actual values are close to zero.
A model that matches the training data very closely but forecasts new data poorly. It often has too many parameters. Hold-out testing and AIC or BIC help you detect it.
The correlation between a series and its lag k after the effect of the lags in between is removed. A sharp cutoff after lag p suggests an AR(p) model.

The probability of seeing a result at least as extreme as yours if the null hypothesis is true. A small value is evidence against the null hypothesis. It is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true.
The differences between the actual values and the values that the model fitted. A good model leaves residuals that look like white noise.
The square root of the average squared forecast error. It punishes large errors more than MAE does. It is in the same units as the data.
ARIMA with extra seasonal terms. It is written ARIMA(p, d, q)(P, D, Q)s, where s is the length of the season, for example 7 for weekly cycles in daily data.
A pattern that repeats at a fixed period, such as a weekly cycle in energy demand. The period is the seasonal length s.
A series is stationary when its mean, variance, and autocorrelation do not change over time. ARMA models need a stationary series.
A division of the series into an earlier part for fitting and a later part for testing. For time series you split by time, never at random.
A long-term rise or fall in the level of a series.
A feature of a series that makes it non-stationary, as in a random walk. Shocks never fade away. Differencing removes a unit root.
A series of uncorrelated values with a constant mean and variance. It has no pattern to forecast. Good model residuals look like white noise.
